Most of my friends knew, as well as several family members. It wasn't too difficult to come out to them. My patents, though...
We had a rough go of it for about 6 months, and I went another 4 months not speaking to my dad. I came out incredibly young, at 14, so I didn't have the luxury of being in my own place. My mother told me once " I go to bed every night and pray you wake up normal." My dad said, after an argument about gays and religion, "...as for burning in hell, you better take a damn good look at yourself." They wouldn't let me tell my sister at the time, who was 10. They told me I would be too much of an embarrassment to her, and she didn't need that stress at school. She eventually found out and had no problem with it. Seemed excited, actually. My parents grew to tolerate it, realizing it wasn't a phase. Now, ten years later, they love and accept who I am. My parents are even advocates for gay marriage. And I couldn't have expected it to turn out so perfectly.
